title: How does the 911 system find your location?

lines.text: When you dial nine-one-one from your mobile phone in an emergency, how does the dispatcher pinpoint your location?
lines.caps: How does 911 find you if *you | don't know where you *are?

lines.text: Unlike landlines tied to fixed street addresses, mobile phones move constantly.
lines.caps: Mobile phones move constantly, so *911 | uses advanced *tech

lines.text: When you place the call, cell towers instantly initiate Enhanced 911 protocol.
Your carrier triangulates radio pings from neighboring towers to narrow down your area to a block.
lines.caps: Triangulates tower pings to *narrow | your general *block

lines.text: Simultaneously, modern smartphones activate high-accuracy GPS, Wi-Fi beacons, and barometric sensors.
The barometric pressure sensor measures vertical elevation to tell dispatchers which floor of a high-rise building you are on.
lines.caps: Barometers even tell dispatchers *what | floor of a building you're *on!

lines.text: Always state your exact address first in any emergency to help responders arrive as fast as possible.
lines.caps: Always state your *address | first when dialing *911!
